subject: Geo‑binding and legal egress: detailed impact analysis for RFP
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules.martin@finservcorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finservcorp.com, legal@finservcorp.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFP Q12: geo-binding / egress guarantees and evidence request

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our RFP. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams: can Redwood provide a firm statement on whether customer data originating in the EU can be guaranteed to remain within the EU across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options? Please detail all technical and contractual controls that prevent cross-border egress, and list any scenarios where egress might still occur (e.g., third‑party integrations, DR failover, telemetry).

We also need:
- a matrix of available hosting regions and which product modes they cover (Hosted / Dedicated / Private),
- descriptions of key management options and whether CMEK is available for Hosted, Dedicated, Private,
- evidence pointers (SOC2, tenancy diagrams, network egress matrix CSV), and
- a sample contract clause or rider for a no-export commitment.

Request ID: RFP-FS-2026-0928-Q12
Timeline: would like initial answers by next Tuesday 2026-12-07 so legal can review before our vendor day.

Best,
Jules Martin
Procurement Lead, FinServ Corp
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: RFP Q12: geo-binding / egress guarantees — draft response and artifacts

Team — forwarding FinServ's question. Draft below is my proposed structure for the RFP response. I attached a draft matrix (network-egress-matrix.csv) and our internal data-location brief (redwood-data-locations-2026-11.pdf). Please review and flag any legal/ops inaccuracies.

Draft answer (high level):
1) Data residency guarantee
   - Hosted API: customers may select a regional endpoint; data at rest is stored in the selected region for active workloads. However, Hosted customers do not get a contractual CMEK by default.
   - Dedicated: we can provision dedicated GPU pools in an EU region (contractually bound to keep customer data within the region). Add a contractual 'no-export' rider and explicit SLA about region residency.
   - Private: full control; all data paths remain on-customer network unless customer authorizes cross-border replication.

2) Egress scenarios (when data could cross borders)
   - Customer-initiated exports (explicit exports to third parties)
   - Cross-region failover for DR — by default disabled unless customer signs DR waiver
   - Model variant fallback to a cheaper region during capacity shortages — off by default; can be prevented by policy config
   - Telemetry and aggregated metrics (can be minimized/pseudonymized or disabled)

3) Controls & mitigations
   - VPC-level gateways, private peering, and strict routing policies,
   - CMEK for Dedicated/Private (we will document supported KMS providers),
   - Audit logs with egress event records and retention aligned to compliance needs,
   - Contract clause examples attached.

Action items:
- Marissa: please review the contractual language and confirm if we can offer a hard 'no-export' rider for Dedicated (and sample wording).
- Karthik: confirm operational limits for Dedicated provisioning in eu-west-1 and whether DR replication is ever enabled by default.

I suggest we send the formal reply from me with Karthik and Marissa cc'd.

Eve
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: RFP Q12: geo-binding / egress guarantees and evidence request

Hi Jules — thanks for the clear list. Below are our consolidated answers and the evidence pointers. I'm happy to walk through these on a short call.

SUMMARY (short answers)
1) Can EU-origin data be guaranteed to remain in the EU?
   - Hosted API: Region selection ensures data-at-rest and inference processing occur in the selected region. We encrypt data at rest and in transit. For Hosted customers requiring contractual CMEK we recommend Dedicated.
   - Dedicated: Yes — we will commit to data residency in contract for Dedicated capacity provisioned in the customer's chosen EU region. We can add a contractual 'no-export' rider and specify permitted exceptions (e.g., court order).
   - Private: Yes — customer has full control; Redwood's control plane can be hosted in customer VPC or on-prem and configured to avoid cross-border communication.

2) Concrete egress scenarios and default behaviors
   - Customer-initiated exports: always explicit and auditable; no automatic exports.
   - DR failover: cross-region DR is disabled by default. We only enable cross-region replication with explicit customer approval. If enabled, it will be listed in the contract with an allowed target region.
   - Model fallback: routing policies may route to compatible model variants; this feature is off by default for customers that require strict geo-binding. We can enforce per-customer routing policy to prevent fallback outside the region.
   - Telemetry & metrics: network-level and per-token metrics are collected for platform health. For sensitive customers we offer reduced telemetry (aggregate-only) or opt-out for telemetry collection; audit logs with egress events are available and can be retained in-region.

3) Key management and encryption
   - Hosted API: platform-managed keys by default. We can discuss Hosted CMEK options on a case-by-case basis but recommend Dedicated for strict CMEK requirements.
   - Dedicated & Private: support for customer-managed keys (CMEK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM integrations. Keys and key policies are scoped to the tenant and region.

4) Legal & contractual controls
   - We will provide a sample 'no-export' rider for use with Dedicated contracts. The rider will enumerate permitted exceptions (e.g., lawful process) and specify remedy and audit rights.

5) Evidence and artifacts (attached/linked)
   - redwood-data-locations-2026-11.pdf (detailed region map and architectural notes) — attached
   - network-egress-matrix.csv (enumerates egress types and default geographic scope) — attached
   - SOC 2 Type II report (available under NDA) — link provided upon request
   - Runbook link for operations: https://drive.redwood.com/s/efs8k-data-egress-policy

If FinServ needs hardline contractual language, we can draft a proposed amendment and run it through Legal. Let me know if you want a call; I'm available next week Wednesday/Thursday afternoons.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

2) For telemetry: we need a statement that raw request/response bodies will never leave the EU for customers that select EU-only handling. Aggregated metrics are fine but only if they are pseudonymized and stored in-region.

If you can confirm those two items in writing we can proceed to the contract mark-up stage. Would also appreciate a 20-minute call; are you available 2026-12-08 14:00 CET?

Thanks,
